redBeforeFix: vitest -t 1691 on origin/main source (2f6817f9): 3 failed | 2 passed -- the three comment cases returned no VAC-002 (expected ['counts'], got []); the two negative guards passed. Re-confirmed red by reverting only vacuity-scanner.ts after the fix (3 failed), green with it (161/161 in the file). Review follow-up (Python must-fix): the four 'in a Python body' tests ran against 96862833: 2 failed | 2 passed -- floor division `assert 10 // target(5) == 2` gave a false VAC-002 (['test_t'], expected []), and a trailing `# target(1)` gave no VAC-002 (expected ['test_t']); the two guards (trailing # after a real call, # inside a string) passed. Green after threading the language flag (165/165 in the file).
assumptions: Human decision: one shared, quote-aware comment definition (commentSpans/isComment) used by both the VAC-002 body filter and the @covers annotation walk (attachesToDeclaration); the separate s.startsWith('/*') check is removed.
Trailing // and /* ... */ spans are blanked offset-preserving from both the blanked text and the raw line, so VAC-001 and the other rules also stop reading comment tails.

commentSpans/isComment/codeLines take the scanner's python flag. Python: only a quote-aware # opens a comment, to end of line (// is floor division, /* is not a token), so a trailing # comment after code IS now stripped. JS/TS: unchanged -- a line starting with # or * is whole-line comment, // to end, /* ... */ spans cut out.
A /* opened on a line and closed on a later line is stripped to end of line; continuation lines that do not start with * are still read as code (pre-existing, out of scope).
Behaviour change at the annotation walk: a line '/* x */ code()' no longer attaches to the declaration below it, because it holds code.
Measured on canary's own ts/test: findings unchanged (215); skipped 577 -> 579, two tests whose body ran into a /** ... */ opener naming the target now abstain (deeper) instead of passing as invoked.
